idiom_name: struct PersonRow: FetchableRecord, MutablePersistableRecord with insert/update/delete
implementation_notes: GRDB gives the row protocol conformances instead of a hand-written class: a struct conforming to FetchableRecord and MutablePersistableRecord is fetched with PersonRow.fetchOne(db, key: 1) and persists itself with try row.insert(db) / try row.update(db) / try row.delete(db) (upsert and save variants exist too). The record stays a plain Codable value type and the database queue supplies the connection, so the classic gateway structure is provided by the library - which is the norm on Apple platforms.
pitfalls: Persistence methods must run inside a database reader/writer access; calling them on a record outside dbQueue.write/read traps or throws.
Records are structs: insert mutates the copy it is called on, so the id assigned by the database is lost unless the mutated value is kept.
Decoding is Codable-based, so a column not present in the row makes the whole fetch fail unless it is optional.

variants.name: Vapor Fluent Model class with save(on:)/find(on:)
variants.implementation_notes: Fluent models the row as a class: a final class conforming to Model declares @ID and @Field property wrappers, and persistence is row-centric - try await row.save(on: db) inserts or updates depending on whether the id is set, while PersonRow.find(id, on: db) and .query(on: db).filter(...).first() act as the finder. This is the idiomatic choice inside a Vapor service because the same model can be used for migrations and relations, at the price of reference semantics and an ORM that also provides query building and relations beyond the gateway role.
variants.idiom_name: final class PersonRow: Model with save(on:)/find(on:)/delete(on:)
pitfalls: save(on:) silently decides insert vs update from the id, so forgetting to set the id after an insert creates duplicates.
Models are reference types shared across tasks: concurrent mutation of one row object is a data race, and Swift 6 strict concurrency requires confinement or Sendable conformances.
Field keys must match the schema exactly; a typo surfaces only at runtime as a missing-column error.
